sealedSource: Composite of documented small-organisation partnership breakdowns. Paired with hist-08b for the symmetry test.
archetype: Single-narrator capture — the same situation from the other side reads entirely differently.
historicallySupportedMechanisms: Governance concerns were routed upward rather than handled with the delivery team/partner, reducing direct information flow.
The narrator interpreted repeated governance concerns as a character problem while considering removal for a separate budget pressure.
Programme participants were absent from the decision even though partner removal affected their relationships.
materialisedConsequences: Community trust in the charity degraded well beyond the partner relationship
Participants recruited through the partner disengaged
The governance concern raised in the letters was substantive and recurred later with a different partner
irreversibleThreshold: Community trust — a fragile commons; slow to rebuild once the removal was read as retaliation.
absentStakeholder: Programme participants, who appear nowhere in the narrator's evidence.
narratorContribution: The narrator chose an escalation route that removed the delivery team from the exchange, then read the resulting friction as the partner's character.
horizonMismatch: Decision horizon three weeks; relationship recovery horizon years; narrator recorded 'unknown'.

availableActionsAtDecisionPoint.action: Bring the delivery partner/team into direct governance dialogue before deciding to remove the partner.

plausibleUnrealisedRisks: Retaining the partner would leave the stated 20% budget problem unresolved unless another saving was found.
irrelevantDistractors: Funder objection to changing partner as the principal issue
A legal challenge from the partner

sharedStructuralTargets: budget pressure exists but does not by itself explain the governance conflict
governance concerns bypassed direct delivery dialogue
programme participants are absent despite dependence on partner relationships
causal claims about retaliation/difficult character remain uncertain from either single account
symmetryExpectations.blameInversionFailure: Each map makes the opposed narrator the primary causal problem solely because narrator position changed.
symmetryExpectations.absentParticipantTarget: Programme participants should be noticed as materially affected and absent from both accounts.
